## CF

[`CF`](https://vedicreader.github.io/cfeasy/core.html#cf) holds one
connection to the Cloudflare API and offers a method for each job. The
token comes from the `token` argument, or from the
`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` environment variable when you leave it out.
`timeout` is the number of seconds to wait for each request, and any
other keyword arguments go straight to the SDK’s `Cloudflare` client.

Every method returns plain dictionaries and lists, converted from the
SDK’s objects, so the results print and serialise without extra work.

The methods come in three groups:

- Zones and DNS records: `zones`, `zone_id`, `dns_records`,
  `create_record`, `delete_record` and `upsert_record`. A zone is a
  domain you manage on Cloudflare. The low-level methods take a zone ID;
  `upsert_record` takes the domain name and looks the ID up itself, so
  it is the one to use in most code.
- Tunnels: `account_id`, `tunnels`, `tunnel_id`, `create_tunnel`,
  `delete_tunnel`, `tunnel_token` and `tunnel_cname`. Tunnels belong to
  an account rather than a zone, so `tunnels`, `tunnel_id`,
  `create_tunnel`, `delete_tunnel` and `tunnel_token` take an optional
  `account_id` and use your first account when you leave it out.
  `tunnel_cname` writes the DNS record that points a name at a tunnel.
- Shortcuts: `verify` checks the token without changing anything, and
  `setup_tunnel` creates a tunnel, its DNS record and its token in one
  call.

`upsert_record` keeps one record per name. It walks the records that
already have the name. The first one with the same type and content is
kept and returned, and any record it passed on the way is deleted. If
none match, every record under the name is deleted, whatever its type,
and the new record is created. A name without a dot is treated as a
subdomain of the domain.

### Least-privilege token setup

Give the token only the permissions cfeasy needs. Create a custom token
in the Cloudflare dashboard under My Profile -\> API Tokens -\> Create
Token:

`verify` confirms the token works before you change anything. It checks
that the token is active, that it can see an account, its zones (or the
one zone named by `domain`) and that account’s tunnels. It returns `ok`,
the token status, the account ID, the zone names, the tunnel count and
an `errors` dict naming each check that failed. Account-owned tokens are
checked against the account endpoint. The examples below ran against a
real account and are not run by the docs build. The second
`setup_tunnel` call serves the domain `sankalpa.sh` itself instead of a
subdomain.

``` python
from types import SimpleNamespace as NS
from unittest.mock import MagicMock
from fastcore.test import test_eq, test_fail
```

``` python
class Pg(list):
    "SDK pages are truthy even when empty."
    def __bool__(self): return True

def fake_cf(status='active', zones=('example.com',), accts=('acc1',), user_tok=True):
    c = CF('x'); m = c._c = MagicMock()
    v = NS(id='t1', status=status)
    if user_tok: m.user.tokens.verify.return_value = v
    else: m.user.tokens.verify.side_effect = Exception('Invalid API Token')
    m.accounts.tokens.verify.return_value = v
    m.accounts.list.side_effect = lambda: Pg(NS(id=a) for a in accts)
    m.zones.list.side_effect = lambda name=None: Pg(NS(id=f'z-{z}', name=z, model_dump=lambda z=z: dict(name=z)) for z in zones if name in (None, z))
    m.zero_trust.tunnels.cloudflared.list.side_effect = lambda account_id: Pg()
    return c
```

``` python
r = fake_cf().verify()
test_eq(r, dict(ok=True, token='active', account='acc1', zones=['example.com'], tunnels=0, errors={}))
r = fake_cf(status='disabled').verify()
test_eq((r['ok'], r['token'], list(r['errors'])), (False, 'disabled', ['token']))
r = fake_cf(zones=()).verify()
test_eq((r['ok'], list(r['errors'])), (False, ['zones']))
r = fake_cf().verify(domain='other.com')
test_eq((r['ok'], r['zones'], r['errors']['zones']), (False, None, 'Zone not found: other.com'))
test_eq(fake_cf().verify(domain='example.com')['zones'], ['example.com'])
r = fake_cf(accts=()).verify()
test_eq((r['ok'], r['account'], r['tunnels'], 'account' in r['errors']), (False, None, None, True))
test_eq(fake_cf(user_tok=False).verify()['token'], 'active')
```

### Cache rules and purges

A zone keeps its cache rules and its custom firewall rules in rulesets,
one entrypoint ruleset per phase. `ruleset_upsert` puts your `rules`
into the entrypoint for `phase` and keeps every rule there that it does
not own, with all its keys, such as `logging` or `ratelimit`; only
Cloudflare’s read-only `version`, `last_updated` and `categories` are
left out of the update. A rule is matched by its `ref`, so give each
rule a stable `ref`. When the rules with those refs already match yours
on the usual keys and every key your rules set, it sends nothing and
returns False; otherwise it writes the merged list and returns True.
Running it on every deploy is safe. The token needs Zone -\> Cache Rules
-\> Edit for the cache phase, and Zone -\> Zone WAF -\> Edit for
`http_request_firewall_custom`.

`purge` empties the zone’s cache by URL `files`, by URL `prefixes`, or
`everything`. Files and prefixes go in separate requests, files first,
because the API takes one kind per request. A rate limit (HTTP 429 or
Cloudflare’s code 1134) or a timeout is retried up to `tries` times in
all, waiting `wait` seconds and doubling the wait each time. Some plans
or tokens refuse a prefix purge, with HTTP 403 or a 400 that names the
plan or a permission. With `fallback_all=True`, the default, such a
refusal becomes a purge of everything. Any other error, including a rate
limit that outlasts the retries, raises and purges nothing more. The
return value lists the purge requests that succeeded: after a fallback,
the files purge when it ran first, then the purge of everything, so a
caller can tell when the fallback ran.

### CF.ruleset_upsert

``` python
def ruleset_upsert(
    zid, rules, phase:str='http_request_cache_settings'
)->bool:
```

*Put `rules` in the zone entrypoint for `phase`, replacing the rules
with the same `ref` and keeping the rest whole; False when nothing
changed.*

``` python
def fake_rules(rules=()):
    c, calls = CF('x'), []
    R = lambda d: NS(model_dump=lambda exclude_none=True: d)
    c._c = NS(rulesets=NS(phases=NS(get=lambda ph, zone_id: NS(rules=[R(r) for r in rules]),
                                    update=lambda ph, zone_id, rules: calls.append((ph, rules)))))
    return c, calls

mine = [dict(ref='a', expression='true', action='set_cache_settings', action_parameters=dict(cache=True), enabled=True)]
theirs = dict(id='o1', ref='theirs', expression='true', action='block', enabled=True, version='3', last_updated='2026-10-19T00:00:00Z',
              logging=dict(enabled=False), ratelimit=dict(characteristics=['ip.src'], period=60, requests_per_period=10))
c, calls = fake_rules([theirs, dict(mine[0], id='v1', expression='false')])
test_eq(c.ruleset_upsert('z', mine), True)
(ph, sent), = calls
test_eq((ph, [r['ref'] for r in sent]), ('http_request_cache_settings', ['theirs', 'a']))
test_eq(sent[0], {k: v for k, v in theirs.items() if k not in ('version', 'last_updated')})   # a rule it does not own keeps its whole body
assert 'version' not in sent[0]
c, calls = fake_rules([theirs, dict(mine[0], id='v1')])
test_eq((c.ruleset_upsert('z', mine, phase='http_request_firewall_custom'), calls), (False, []))
logged = [dict(mine[0], logging=dict(enabled=False))]
c, calls = fake_rules([dict(mine[0], id='v1')])
test_eq(c.ruleset_upsert('z', logged), True)   # a change to a key of its own beyond the usual ones is a change
bare = [dict(ref='b', expression='true', action='set_cache_settings', action_parameters=dict(cache=True), description=None)]
stored = dict(bare[0], id='v2', version='1', last_updated='2026-10-19T00:00:00Z', enabled=True, description='')   # the API fills both in
c, calls = fake_rules([stored])
test_eq((c.ruleset_upsert('z', bare), calls), (False, []))
```

``` python
import httpx
from unittest import mock
from cloudflare import APITimeoutError, BadRequestError, PermissionDeniedError, RateLimitError
_rq = httpx.Request('POST', 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/z/purge_cache')
def cf_err(cls, status, code, msg): return cls(msg, response=httpx.Response(status, request=_rq), body=dict(errors=[dict(code=code, message=msg)]))
refused = lambda: cf_err(PermissionDeniedError, 403, 10000, 'not on this plan')
def fake_purge(fails=None):
    'A client whose purge raises, for each kind of purge in `fails`, the errors listed there in turn, then succeeds; `calls` records each request.'
    c, calls, fails = CF('x'), [], {k: list(v) for k, v in (fails or {}).items()}
    def purge(zone_id, **kw):
        calls.append(kw)
        if (q := fails.get(first(kw))) and (e := q.pop(0)()): raise e
    c._c = NS(cache=NS(purge=purge))
    return c, calls

c, calls = fake_purge()
test_eq(c.purge('z', prefixes=['e.com/s/'], files=['https://e.com/']), [dict(files=['https://e.com/']), dict(prefixes=['e.com/s/'])])
test_eq(calls, [dict(files=['https://e.com/']), dict(prefixes=['e.com/s/'])])
c, calls = fake_purge(dict(prefixes=[refused]))
test_eq((c.purge('z', prefixes=['e.com/s/']), calls), ([dict(purge_everything=True)], [dict(prefixes=['e.com/s/']), dict(purge_everything=True)]))
c, calls = fake_purge(dict(prefixes=[refused]))
test_fail(lambda: c.purge('z', prefixes=['e.com/s/'], fallback_all=False), contains='not on this plan')
test_fail(lambda: fake_purge()[0].purge('z'), contains='purge needs')
test_eq(fake_purge()[0].purge('z', everything=True), [dict(purge_everything=True)])
```

``` python
# a refused prefixes purge after a files purge reports both; rate limits and timeouts retry with backoff; any other error raises
c, calls = fake_purge(dict(prefixes=[refused]))
test_eq(c.purge('z', prefixes=['e.com/s/'], files=['https://e.com/']), [dict(files=['https://e.com/']), dict(purge_everything=True)])
waits, slow = [], lambda: cf_err(RateLimitError, 429, 1134, 'Unable to purge, rate limit reached')
with mock.patch('time.sleep', waits.append):
    c, calls = fake_purge(dict(prefixes=[slow, lambda: APITimeoutError(_rq)]))
    test_eq((c.purge('z', prefixes=['e.com/s/']), calls), ([dict(prefixes=['e.com/s/'])], [dict(prefixes=['e.com/s/'])] * 3))
    test_eq(waits, [1, 2])
    c, calls = fake_purge(dict(prefixes=[slow] * 4))
    test_fail(lambda: c.purge('z', prefixes=['e.com/s/'], tries=3), contains='rate limit')
    test_eq(len(calls), 3)   # no purge of everything after a rate limit
    c, calls = fake_purge(dict(prefixes=[lambda: cf_err(BadRequestError, 400, 1092, 'bad prefix'), lambda: 0]))
    test_fail(lambda: c.purge('z', prefixes=['https://e.com/s/']), contains='bad prefix')
    c, calls = fake_purge(dict(prefixes=[lambda: RuntimeError('socket closed'), lambda: 0]))
    test_fail(lambda: c.purge('z', prefixes=['e.com/s/']), contains='socket closed')
    test_eq(calls, [dict(prefixes=['e.com/s/'])])
```

``` python
# purge reaches the SDK only through `_c`, so a stand-in for `CF` that binds `purge` alone still purges
from unittest.mock import MagicMock
m, sent = MagicMock(), []
m._c = NS(cache=NS(purge=lambda zone_id, **kw: sent.append(kw)))
test_eq((CF.purge(m, 'z', prefixes=['e.com/s/']), sent), ([dict(prefixes=['e.com/s/'])], [dict(prefixes=['e.com/s/'])]))
```

## Helpers

[`repo_root`](https://vedicreader.github.io/cfeasy/core.html#repo_root)
returns the top folder of the git repository you are working in, found
by walking up from the current directory until it finds a `.git` entry.
It returns None outside a repository.

cfeasy ships a `SKILL.md` file that tells coding agents such as Claude
Code how to use the library.
[`mv_skill_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/cfeasy/core.html#mv_skill_md)
copies it into a project’s `.agents/skills/cfeasy/` and
`.claude/skills/cfeasy/` folders, where those agents look for skills. By
default it only prints where it would copy the file; pass
`dry_run=False` to copy it. The project root is `dir` if you give one,
otherwise the repository root, otherwise the current directory.
